decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in economic activity appears to have picked up.
changes.explanation: The Fed notes that job market progress has slowed down, even though overall economic activity picked up.

changes.quote: Although the unemployment rate has declined, job gains have diminished.
changes.explanation: While the jobless rate dropped, the number of new jobs being added has gotten smaller.

changes.quote: Growth in household spending has strengthened.
changes.explanation: Consumers are spending more strongly than before.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined; most survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recent months.
changes.explanation: Market measures showing expected inflation have dropped recently.

changes.quote: Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Janet L. Yellen, Chair; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Stanley Fischer; Esther L. George; Loretta J. Mester; Jerome H. Powell; Eric Rosengren; and Daniel K. Tarullo.
changes.explanation: Esther L. George joined the voting roster for this meeting.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in economic activity appears to have picked up.
Although the unemployment rate has declined, job gains have diminished.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.31% APR costs about $51.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.6% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.66% would fall by about $3.38 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.8%, and employers added an average of 165k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (May 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.19% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate increases will be gradual as the Committee monitors inflation and job growth.

citations.detail: Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
